newsitem.title: IRAQ: Syrian traders in Iraq to sell food, medicine.
newsitem.headline: Syrian traders in Iraq to sell food, medicine.

text.p: A team of Syrian businessmen arrived in Baghdad on Monday hoping to sell Iraq foodstuffs and medicines and buy crude under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

The delegation's leader Rateb al-Shallah, chairman of Syria's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, described his visit as a step towards better ties between the two countries, ruled by rival factions of the Arab Baath party.
He said Syrian traders were willing to sell Iraq goods "in accordance with the memorandum of understanding".
"Why should Iraq buy from thousands of miles away when we have these products which would cost them less and reach them more quickly?" Rateb told Reuters.

Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Asked if Syria would be interested in buying Iraqi oil, he said: "Why not?"
"This is a courtesy visit and I think it must be the beginning of new era of cooperation," Rateb said.
Baghdad's ties with Damascus were severed in 1980 when Syria sided with Iran in the 1980-1988 Iran-Iraq War.
Relations further worsened in 1990 when Syria joined a U.S.-led multinational force which ejected Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.
Syria has been abiding by the trade sanctions imposed on Iraq for invading Kuwait in 1990.
"There is no reason why we should not deal with each other...in accordance with international laws," Rateb added.
He said the Syrian government allowed the visit, the first since the two countries ruptured ties in the early 1980s.

"Our government has no objection to allowing us (to visit Iraq)," said Rateb who drove with six other leading Syrian businessmen along the highway from Damascus to Baghdad, which has been closed since the early 1980s when the states severed diplomatic ties.
